_doc: Studio-level work that isn't a single episode stage (engine, assets, tools). `python3 studio/studio.py next` reads this together with the episodes. status: todo | doing | done | blocked. who: model | human | laptop (needs the user's GPU machine). done_when: a command whose exit code 0 proves the task is done (optional). Update status and notes when you finish; never mark done without the done_when check passing.

tasks.title: Build `python3 studio/studio.py dashboard` -> docs/dashboard.html
tasks.detail: studio.py already dispatches `dashboard` to studio/dashboard.py:build(root) (not written yet). One self-contained HTML page (no external assets except Google Fonts), readable on a phone, light and dark: per channel (bible status, open_decisions, music tracks approved/pending), every episode with its 10 stages (passed/pending/failed/stale, from studio.py's state functions), the backlog grouped by who (model/human/laptop), and the open + blocked lists from docs/DECISIONS.md. Regenerate it whenever state changes and commit it.

tasks.title: Promote the Point Roberts v2 diorama into catalog scene types
tasks.detail: episodes/why-map/point-roberts/scenes.js is the new standard. Lift its reusable parts into studio/engine so cheaper agents can use them without writing code: a side-view world (sky, mountains, water, ground, road, near foreground with fence, bushes and edge pines), vehicles (car, top-down car, bus), border booth with barrier, waving flags (US, CA, then any flag from flags.js), people, a crowd-count scene (N figures that thin out), a map with a moving vehicle along a route and an odometer, a cutaway (pipe under a border), a shopfront row whose windows go dark, a desk-and-parchment history beat. Each becomes a catalog type with params and word cues.
tasks.done_when: A new why-map episode can reach the Point Roberts v2 frozen-time bar (<=1 s per 30 s, hold <=0.6 s) using catalog types only, with custom scenes under 20%.
